subject: NexusBridge on‑prem deployment: ops ownership, storage fallback & archive strategy

To: Danielle Price <danielle.price@nexusbridge.com>, Alex Moore <amoore@nb-sys.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: NexusBridge on‑prem deployment: ops ownership, storage fallback & archive strategy

Hi Danielle / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, I’m attaching an initial ops responsibility matrix and a sketch of the archive/fallback flow we’ll need to validate with your infra team. I want to make sure we have alignment on three things before we lock dates for the site readiness window: 

1) Who owns day‑to‑day node pool scaling and emergency hotfixes on site (NexusBridge on‑call vs Redwood ops).
2) The archival retention flow (hot NVMe -> warm block -> offline tape/air‑gapped export) and the criteria that trigger each tier.
3) The exact list of network egress controls and whether the customer firewall requires explicit CIDR allow rules for KV‑cache warming traffic.

Ask: please confirm preferred ops owner and any constraints on outbound ports by EOD Monday so Karthik and Irene can finalize the runbook.

Attachments: nexusbridge-site-ops-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (XLSX), nb-archive-flow-diagram_v3.pdf (PDF), runbook-handback-checklist.md (MD)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415‑555‑0199

--
Redwood Inference — Developer‑first inference platform

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: NexusBridge on‑prem deployment: ops ownership, storage fallback & archive strategy

Jordan —

Appreciate the notes and the docs. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Ops ownership: NexusBridge will own rack‑level maintenance, hardware replacement, and KVM access. We’d prefer Redwood to own the application‑level rolling upgrades, model rollbacks, and KV cache priming during business hours for the first 90 days post‑cutover. After 90 days we’ll revisit SLA split.

- Archive flow: the diagram looks right conceptually. Two asks: (a) retention slices need to be enforceable via RBAC in the cluster (we cannot rely on an external ad‑hoc script), and (b) we require a short audit trail for any archive exports (who triggered, what was exported).

- Network: our security team requires explicit outbound CIDR rules; I’ll attach a short list tomorrow. For now assume only 443 and a restricted UDP range for monitoring.

One other thing — can Redwood provide a suggested ops escalation ladder (names/roles) for the first 30 days? We’d like to include it in our procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Danielle
Head of Infrastructure, NexusBridge Systems
Danielle.Price@nexusbridge.com | +1 617‑555‑0043

Thanks for the context — adding some engineering detail and a proposed runbook excerpt below. I’m including the runbook excerpt as plain text here for quick review; full MD is attached.

Runbook excerpt (abridged):
- PRE‑CUTOVER (2 weeks out): verify node labels, taints for inference pods, PV classes mapped (fast-nvme, warm-block), and kubelet eviction thresholds at 80%/90%/95%.
- CUTOVER DAY: Redwood to perform model priming sequence during business hours (09:00–17:00 local) while NexusBridge infra performs network ACL verification. Model priming uses ephemeral jobs that write to fast-nvme and warm‑block to validate I/O plumbing.
- POST‑CUTOVER (0–90 days): Redwood owns application fixes, can apply non‑disruptive upgrades. NexusBridge owns firmware, disk replacement, and power resets. Joint on‑call: NexusBridge infra + Redwood SRE on pager for 30 days.

Archive & export guardrails:
- Exports must be requested via RBACed k8s custom resource (ArchiveRequest). Requests log user, namespace, object list, time.
- Automated tiering policy: if object last accessed > 45 days -> warm block; > 365 days -> offline export candidate. Admin approval required for physical export.

Network egress notes: KV cache prefill contact endpoints: cache-prime.redwood.ai:443 (we will provide a CIDR list for peering). Metrics/monitoring uses port 9125 UDP and 443 TCP.

I’ll prepare an escalation ladder draft and a sample PagerDuty rotation for the first 30 days. Karthik — can you confirm commercial coverage for the 90‑day post cutover window so Marissa can complete the SOW language?

Irene Choi
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
